flows.brief:
# Flow `treffen-mit-terminen-anlegen` — Treffen mit Terminen anlegen
Der Organisator legt ein Treffen an und erfasst gleich mehrere Terminvorschläge dazu, damit der Link verschickt werden kann.

## Your hook — import it, never rebuild what it owns
`import { useTreffenMitTerminenAnlegenFlow } from '@/lib/journey/flows/TreffenMitTerminenAnlegen';` — generated from the Schreibliste below. It OWNS the form(s), one record search per picked field (columns and filter from the plan) and the submit plan with every fixed and derived value. You compose: `flow.forms.<entity>` for <Bound>/<Field>, `{...flow.picks.<field>.select} {...flow.pick('<field>')}` (or `flow.pickMany` for a multi pick) for <EntitySelectStep>, `flow.validateStep(n)` in StepNav.onNext, `flow.submit` + `flow.formList` for SummaryStep/SuccessStep, `flow.reset()`; what the hook does not own reads through its door `flow.port` — availability `useOccupancy(flow.port, '<entity>', { resource })`, a count `useRecordCount(flow.port, …)` — never import servicePort next to the hook. Options: `steps` (field → step), `items` (how a hit reads, per pick: treffen), `initial`, `messages`. The hook's docblock in .lane-context.md shows the exact call. Never import servicePort, useStepForm, useJourneySubmit, useRecordSearch or useDashboardData in this page — check-intents refuses a page that uses the hook and any of them.

## Steps (in this order)
1. Titel, Ort, Beschreibung und Namen des Organisators eingeben
2. Einen oder mehrere Terminvorschläge mit Datum und Uhrzeit erfassen
3. Treffen speichern, Status ist automatisch „Offen“

## Schreibliste — the ONLY writes this flow makes (the gate compares your plan steps with this list)
- creates `treffen`:
    - `titel`: the user enters it (bind it through the layer: form.field/…)
    - `beschreibung`: the user enters it (bind it through the layer: form.field/…)
    - `ort`: the user enters it (bind it through the layer: form.field/…)
    - `organisator_vorname`: the user enters it (bind it through the layer: form.field/…)
    - `organisator_nachname`: the user enters it (bind it through the layer: form.field/…)
    - `status`: fixed value `offen` — set it in the plan step's values, never ask
- creates `terminvorschlaege`:
    - `treffen`: from the record the user picks in this flow
    - `termin`: the user enters it (bind it through the layer: form.field/…)
    - `anmerkung`: the user enters it (bind it through the layer: form.field/…)

## Success page
- shows: `treffen.titel`, `terminvorschlaege.termin`
- next flows to offer: `termin-festlegen`

## Never write these — another flow or a tool owns them
- `treffen.festgelegter_termin` (owner: intent `termin-festlegen`)

# Flow `termin-festlegen` — Termin festlegen
Der Organisator sieht je Terminvorschlag, wer kann, wählt einen Termin und setzt das Treffen auf „Termin festgelegt“.

## Your hook — import it, never rebuild what it owns
`import { useTerminFestlegenFlow } from '@/lib/journey/flows/TerminFestlegen';` — generated from the Schreibliste below. It OWNS the form(s), one record search per picked field (columns and filter from the plan) and the submit plan with every fixed and derived value. You compose: `flow.forms.<entity>` for <Bound>/<Field>, `{...flow.picks.<field>.select} {...flow.pick('<field>')}` (or `flow.pickMany` for a multi pick) for <EntitySelectStep>, `flow.validateStep(n)` in StepNav.onNext, `flow.submit` + `flow.formList` for SummaryStep/SuccessStep, `flow.reset()`; what the hook does not own reads through its door `flow.port` — availability `useOccupancy(flow.port, '<entity>', { resource })`, a count `useRecordCount(flow.port, …)` — never import servicePort next to the hook. Options: `steps` (field → step), `items` (how a hit reads, per pick), `initial`, `messages`. The hook's docblock in .lane-context.md shows the exact call. This flow CHANGES a record of `treffen`: `{...flow.picks.treffen.select} {...flow.pick('treffen')}` picks it, the hook prefills the form with its current values and updates THAT record — never a create step, never a list from useDashboardData. Never import servicePort, useStepForm, useJourneySubmit, useRecordSearch or useDashboardData in this page — check-intents refuses a page that uses the hook and any of them.

## Steps (in this order)
1. Offenes Treffen auswählen
2. Terminvorschläge mit den Rückmeldungen ansehen
3. Einen Terminvorschlag auswählen
4. Termin übernehmen und Status setzen

## Schreibliste — the ONLY writes this flow makes (the gate compares your plan steps with this list)
- updates `treffen`:
    - `festgelegter_termin`: the user enters it (bind it through the layer: form.field/…)
    - `status`: fixed value `termin_festgelegt` — set it in the plan step's values, never ask

## Reads
- `treffen` columns titel, ort, status
- `terminvorschlaege` columns treffen, termin, anmerkung
- `rueckmeldungen` columns teilnehmer_vorname, teilnehmer_nachname, terminvorschlag, antwort, kommentar

## Checks BEFORE the write (block the submit with the message when they fail)
- custom (rule=`Das Treffen muss den Status Offen haben, damit ein Termin festgelegt werden kann`, field=`treffen.status`) — message: „Für dieses Treffen ist bereits ein Termin festgelegt oder es wurde abgesagt.“

## Success page
- shows: `treffen.festgelegter_termin`, `treffen.status`

## Never write these — another flow or a tool owns them
- `treffen.titel` (owner: intent `treffen-mit-terminen-anlegen`)
- `treffen.beschreibung` (owner: intent `treffen-mit-terminen-anlegen`)
- `treffen.ort` (owner: intent `treffen-mit-terminen-anlegen`)
- `treffen.organisator_vorname` (owner: intent `treffen-mit-terminen-anlegen`)
- `treffen.organisator_nachname` (owner: intent `treffen-mit-terminen-anlegen`)
- `terminvorschlaege.treffen` (owner: intent `treffen-mit-terminen-anlegen`)
- `terminvorschlaege.termin` (owner: intent `treffen-mit-terminen-anlegen`)
- `terminvorschlaege.anmerkung` (owner: intent `treffen-mit-terminen-anlegen`)

public_pages.brief:
# Public page `termin-abstimmen`
Teilnehmer öffnen den Link ohne Anmeldung, sehen das offene Treffen mit seinen Terminvorschlägen, tragen ihren Namen ein und geben pro Terminvorschlag an, ob sie können (Ja, Vielleicht, Nein), optional mit Kommentar. Es werden nur offene Treffen angezeigt, keine Rückmeldungen anderer Personen.

## Lists (declare exactly these in the surface)
- `treffen`: columns `titel`, `beschreibung`, `ort`, `organisator_vorname`, `organisator_nachname`, filter {"mode": "all", "conditions": [{"field": "status", "op": "eq", "value": "offen"}]}
- `terminvorschlaege`: columns `treffen`, `termin`, `anmerkung`

## Creates (declare exactly these in the surface)
- `rueckmeldungen`: visitor fields `teilnehmer_vorname`, `teilnehmer_nachname`, `terminvorschlag`, `kommentar`; preset_fields {"antwort": "kann"}

## Availability — mechanical, write nothing for it
A picker (`useRecordSearch`) never offers a record another record already takes (a booked slot) — the layer leaves it out. To SHOW booked periods, call `useOccupancy(port, '<entity>')` and hand `blocked` to AvailabilityRangePicker; the integration gives the page exactly that read (dates or the reference, never who booked). Never declare a list of bookings with names or contacts to work availability out yourself.

Publish: yes
